comparison: Perfect agreement on barcoding system development and validation (C13-C23). Both evaluations find the method novel, compelling, and well-documented with appropriate controls. OpenEval emphasizes technical validation details while peer reviewers praise experimental justification and attention to technical caveats.

Partial overlap on barcode diversity claims (C22, C23). OpenEval finds rarefaction analysis sufficient for validation. Peer reviewer raises uncertainty about non-unique barcode handling, requesting confirmation that such barcodes were removed from downstream analysis.

Strong agreement on poor correlation between transcription and progeny production (C1, C2, C5, C58-C62). Both identify this as a major finding well-supported by data. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation while peer reviewers emphasize the significance of the discovery.

Minimal overlap on Gini coefficient (C12). Both evaluations support the heterogeneity quantification. OpenEval groups this with correlation findings while peer reviewers emphasize it as evidence of progeny production heterogeneity.

Complete agreement on NS gene phenotype (C3, C66-C69, C84). Both find the statistical support strong and conclusions well-supported. OpenEval notes the biological interpretation is reasonable though inferential; peer reviewers accept the finding without challenge.

Full agreement on persistent heterogeneity in cells with complete genomes (C4, C77-C79, C88-C89). Both find the data compelling. OpenEval considers the inference about additional factors reasonable; peer reviewers request more speculation about specific viral/cellular mechanisms.

Agreement on transcription heterogeneity observations (C36-C42). Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval notes consistency with prior work; peer reviewers explicitly state these observations reinforce previous studies and are not novel but valid.

Complete agreement on viral genome sequencing results (C43-C47). Both find the data quality adequate and conclusions well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes technical quality controls; peer reviewers praise the detailed methods and accounting for technical caveats.

Strong agreement on progeny heterogeneity quantification (C48-C57, with C12 overlap). Both identify this as a major finding. OpenEval emphasizes the statistical metrics and technical replicates; peer reviewers highlight the biological significance of few cells producing most progeny.

Agreement on incomplete gene expression and progeny production relationship (C63-C65). Both find conclusions well-supported. OpenEval notes the inference is reasonable; peer reviewers request additional detail about which specific genes were not expressed in progeny-producing cells.

Complete agreement on mutation-progeny relationships (C73-C76). Both evaluations support the findings and quantitative correlations. OpenEval emphasizes the statistical approach; peer reviewers accept the distinction between physical and infectious progeny as part of the novel methodology.

Overlap on study limitations (C90-C92). OpenEval finds the limitations appropriately acknowledged and not invalidating main findings. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about reproducibility, noting results appear from a single experiment, though acknowledging limitations are clearly explained.
